title: Afro-Cuban and Caribbean rhythms, guaracha
summary: He says Afro-Cuban rhythms are closer to African; guitars spread through the Caribbean; guaracha is rhythmically closest to Jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Whereas, now the so-called...the other rhythms are strictly more pure African, or they say Afro-Cuban, whichever... The Negro quality, whatever, is in the two series, you know. That would be much closer to the African rhythms there; you know, Brazil, the samba and all that...

Now, the different islands had different approaches. Say, that the Spaniards had the guitar; well, the guitar spread around the Caribbean. Plus, the coconuts...they were beating the coconuts, like the maracas, whichever way they did... They accentuated it.
And closer, more or less, to the African rhythm would be...the Puerto Rican islands had the "guaracha". Guaracha
was more...the most rhythmically close to the American Jazz rhythms -- which it wasn't very close.
